key_insight: REST3D focuses on reconstructing scenes that are not just visually plausible, but physically stable from a single image. The key idea is to turn casual photos into 3D assets that behave realistically in simulation, reducing issues like floating objects and penetration.
problem_solved: Single-image 3D reconstruction methods often recover geometry that looks correct but is physically inconsistent. This paper addresses the challenge of inferring a scene structure that supports stable, simulation-ready 3D reconstruction from only one RGB image.
method: Uses a single RGB image as input to reconstruct 3D scene geometry.
Targets physical consistency during reconstruction so objects rest and interact in stable ways.
Produces digital assets intended for downstream simulation, immersion, and content creation workflows.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this work improves the usability of monocular 3D reconstruction for real-world applications where physics matters. It helps bridge the gap between visual reconstruction and asset creation for robotics, AR/VR, and simulation.
visual_elements: Before-and-after comparison showing floating/penetrating objects vs. physically stable reconstruction

paper_title: REST3D: Reconstructing Physically Stable 3D Scenes from a Single Image
paper_authors: Xiaoxuan Ma, Jiashun Wang, Nicolas Ugrinovic, Yehonathan Litman, Kris Kitani
